name: Chothe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog cites only subgrouping/comparative works (Shafer 1968-74; Haokip 2011, 2019; Konnerth 2022); no grammar or phonology of Chothe located

sources.citation: CrossRef / CORE / archive.org / Zenodo / HAL / Shodhganga keyword searches 'Chothe'.
sources.note: Only linguistic hits: Singh 2000 thesis (Shodhganga 10603/105201) and Singh 2009 'Negation in Chothe Grammar'; everything else is anthropology/sociology (Yuhlung Cheithou Charles; Marim) or unrelated persons surnamed Chothe.

sources.citation: Language in India (languageinindia.com), all 301 monthly issue indexes 2001-2026 a full-text search for stress/accent.
sources.note: No article on Chothe found (Aimol, Chiru, Koireng, Tarao papers exist, none on Chothe).

sources.citation: Singh, Hidam Brojen. 2000. A descriptive grammar of Chothe. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Manipur University (supervisor Ch. Yashawanta Singh). xii+338 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/105201 (13 scanned PDFs, no text; scanned here).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.2 Phonology (pp.14-74) lists the suprasegmental phonemes as two tones only (level, falling; sec.2.4 pp.73-74 with minimal pairs); syllables sec.2.3; the words 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the whole thesis (all 13 parts scanned and a full-text search for stress/accent); ch.8 conclusion repeats 'two suprasegmental phonemes.. level tone and falling tone'. Only prosody beyond tone is a generic Trask quote on question intonation in ch.6.

sources.citation: Lotven, Samson. 2023. Tone in South Central Tibeto-Burman. Himalayan Linguistics 22(1): 36-66. doi:10.5070/H922153559 (fn.13).
sources.note: Second-hand, tone only: 'Chothe is described as having a two-way contrast between Level and Falling pitch patterns (Singh 2008: 26).' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.) 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Part III: Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma groups. Calcutta. p.262 'Chote, Muntuk, and Karum'; pp.254-255 'Kyau or Chaw'; pp.263ff 'Purum'.
sources.note: Chote (p.262): 'There are no specimens of the dialects available' - nothing on the language at all. Kyau/Chaw of Arakan (pp.254-5, the entry Glottolog links to chot1239): vocabulary comparison only, nothing on accent. Purum (p.263, separate languoid puru1266): 'We have, however, no information as to where the stress should come' and 'no information with regard to tones'.

sources.note: Modern instrumental-style phonology of Purum, the 'Purum (Chote)' community historically equated with Chothe (Needham 'Purum (Chote) revisited'; Ethnologue: purest Chothe spoken in Purum Khullen); Glottolog files Purum separately as puru1266, so identity must be checked, but it is the likeliest place for an explicit stress/prominence statement for this cluster.
